title: Ob and Yenisey mean seven-day peaks exceeded a shuffled-year mean by 0.80% in 1980-2011, with support that depended on the test
abstract: We tested whether a prior three-river peak association also occurs in the Ob-Yenisey pair that enters the Kara Sea. We used 31 common certified years in ArcticGRO v20261104, from 1980 to 2011. The mean April-August seven-day peak of summed gauge flow was 151,624 cubic metres per second. Independent year pairing within three periods gave an exact mean of 150,417, an excess of 0.80%. The conditional two-sided p value was 0.0374. Five-year pairing gave p = 0.0740, and adjustment across three river pairs gave p = 0.0750. Equal seasonal volumes retained a 0.82% excess. Ob-Lena and Yenisey-Lena point excesses were 0.19% and 2.10%; their difference was not tested. Pair effects cannot be added to explain the earlier three-river result. These data show a small positive point association with support that depends on the test. They do not establish coastal freshwater arrival or a physical cause. Short records, conditional exchangeability, regulation, gauge error and absent travel times limit inference. The package includes code, exact source hashes, aggregate results, all null draws, arithmetic checks and a figure. Raw and record-level data remain external.

display.caption: Observed pair peak excess and conditional shuffled-year reference distributions. The red line marks the observed statistic. These ranges are not effect confidence limits.

citations.reason: Its three-river result sets the new pair-specific question. We use overlapping source data and new code; this is not independent data confirmation.
Its certified common-year scope sets a matched sample for the pair tests.
ArcticGRO Discharge Dataset v20261104; three fixed external CSVs with pinned hashes.
Prior runoff and ocean-budget study motivates seasonal input checks and limits on ocean interpretation.
